verdict.decision_rule: SAFETY_DISCHARGED only if every obligation in the mechanism has an explicit validity contract, every required precondition is established by its callers at the candidate, and no safe interface can cause UB. OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED only if a safe ownership model exists and the residual boundary is identified without an unestablished caller precondition. Otherwise NOT_ESTABLISHED.
verdict.statement: The section-7 criterion-3 whole-closure safety argument is NOT ESTABLISHED at b79. The b79c closures are ACCEPTED and discharge 290/290 obligations at the tool's site level, and the conversions raised the fn-level contract coverage from 220/290 at b78 to 275/290. But only 59 of the 290 obligations were independently re-read at b79 (43 X509/VERIFY_POLICY, 15 RAND_CMS_STORE_KEYFMT, 1 SSL_SESSION); the other 231 are bound by an operation-span content hash whose own claim_scope excludes caller closures. The b78 65-row cohort is not reused, because the src content changed (section 22). Five obligations carry only an operation-level SAFETY block, six rest on inventory contract records, and four have no contract. C_ABI_CONTRACT and BIO remain UNSAFE_OPEN mechanism-wide. The reconversion review leaves D1 (11/12 qualifier-control tests self-satisfying), D2 and D5 open. No Miri/ASan/TSan/Loom/dudect run supports any mechanism at b79. The 99 external safe pub fns that reach unsafe in the mechanism files were not reviewed as safe interfaces, so the reviews do not establish criterion 3 for the safe surface. This verdict is consistent with the closures being measurements of the queue, not promotions.

residuals.statement: 231/290 obligations were not independently re-read at b79; the b78 65-row cohort is invalidated by the src change and not re-established

reconversion review D1: 11 of the 12 qualifier-control tests are self-satisfying (include_str! includes the test module and the needle appears in the assert), so removing `unsafe` from 23 of the 24 converted declarations would not fail any test. D2: the SSL_COMP_get_name const assertion pins only the signature and is not a qualifier control.

D4: send_certificate_request's callers cite only 's is live' and not the stated exclusivity/pending_cipher obligations. D5: OPENSSL_init_ssl's # Safety under-specifies the settings obligations it forwards to OPENSSL_init_crypto.
C_ABI_CONTRACT (5 obligations) and BIO (2) are UNSAFE_OPEN mechanism-wide; the BIO site argument covers only the two empty-body operations in the closure
no Miri (Stacked/Tree Borrows), ASan, TSan, Loom or dudect/ctgrind run at b79; the argument is source/closure-level only
the operation-span content hash explicitly excludes caller closures; caller evidence exists only for the 59 re-read rows

99 external safe pub fns in the seven mechanisms' files reach unsafe; none is itself the subject of a b79 review, so criterion 3 is not established for the safe surface even where the obligation rows are accepted
153 reachable unresolved sites are contract-bounded by public ABI (0 target-bounded, 0 unclassified); they are discharged under section 7 criterion 2, not proven safe by this argument
no secret classification or cleansing audit for the RAND/CMS/PEM/SSL_SESSION sites at b79

the safe-surface numbers are lexical: trait-object dispatch, generics, closures and macro-expanded call edges are not resolved, and re-exports are not followed; the counts are over-approximations of call edges and under-approximations of dynamic dispatch
